(Oh OK. Merry xmas)

posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md: A conventional photopolymer hologram to put on your cell phone screen to protect it. Apparently there's also some computer graphics to interact with the holographic image.

posts.author: Jeffrey Weil
posts.content_md:
I sent them a letter and Bob has it right. It's just a normal poly hologram over a screen. I'm sure the graphics on the screen are in register with the hologram but I wouldn't consider that "interactive". There has to be a back and forth between things for it to really be interactive. 

Only the screen is dynamic, not the hologram. I don't understand how any inanimate object can be considered interactive in any situation.

posts.author: 142laser
posts.content_md: It looks like a creative new way to get lab funding; I don't see anything really new here. Am I missing something? Merry Christmas! Phil

posts.author: Sergio
posts.content_md:
Yes, seems a typical Bayer photopolymer full colour hologram.

They cut exactly on Iphone5 format and apply the polyurethane emulsion sticker onto glass. The film adheres well (PU) but the cleaning of gorilla glass surface is typical CRITICAL.

Nothing new here if you get access to Bayer photopolymer...

posts.author: 142laser
posts.content_md: Yes there is...a new way to get research lab funding to buy materials and hire students! They tell you that is what the money is for really...

posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md:
Did anyone notice that Michael Page is doing this. For those who don't know Michael Page, I believe he was one of the Benton Boys. So, he's certainly aware that it's just a photopolymer covering a standard cell phone. Mammon meet Holography! 

By the way, he's not the only one doing anything like this. Nokia has a patent for an edge lit hologram for cell phones. They came to us a few years back, but our edge lit techniques were not developed then and so they went to someone else. Those who get IHMAs patent list may have noticed that Nokia have now got a patent for the edge-lit cell phone protector.
